lines.text: Harper gasps at the crystal chandeliers while Cole steps across the marble floor with quiet authority.

lines.speaker: HARPER
lines.text: Why is the matriarch of Boston's biggest shipping empire demanding to see a hospital nurse and a garage mechanic?

lines.speaker: COLE
lines.text: Just stay close to me and let me handle my former employers.

lines.speaker: DIANE
lines.text: Look what grease the street cat dragged into my foyer.
Fifty-eight-year-old Diane Whitmore glides down the stairs, sneering at twenty-four-year-old night-shift nurse Harper.

lines.speaker: DIANE
lines.text: Cole paid one hundred thousand dollars for your sister Mia's heart surgery just to buy a fake wife!

lines.speaker: HARPER
lines.text: Cole earned that money at his auto shop, Mrs. Whitmore, and I won't let you insult my husband!
Twenty-nine-year-old sales head Jake Whitmore steps beside Diane, staring at Harper with intense fascination.

lines.speaker: JAKE
lines.text: Don't waste your passion defending a dirty mechanic, Harper, when you could have a real Whitmore man.

scenes.heading: INT. WHITMORE ESTATE - DRAWING ROOM - DAY

lines.text: INT. WHITMORE ESTATE - DRAWING ROOM - DAY
Eighty-one-year-old matriarch Evelyn Whitmore slams her silver cane onto the rug, silencing the room.

lines.speaker: EVELYN
lines.text: Quiet, Jake, before I strip your corporate title away!

lines.speaker: EVELYN
lines.text: Welcome, Harper, to the estate of the man you just legally bound yourself to.

lines.speaker: HARPER
lines.text: Mrs. Whitmore, Cole is just a humble mechanic, so why does our contract marriage matter to you?
Evelyn smiles coldly at Cole, holding up a sealed trust document that requires his marriage to unlock the family shares.
